methodology: M-W etymology research focusing on quality/state nominal suffix -ity
key_difference_from_batch1: Batch 1 (-tion) derives from verbal action nominals. Batch 2 (-ity) derives from adjective quality nominals. Different morphological source = different root forms.

capacity.mwEtymology: Latin capacitas (from capax 'able to hold' + -itas suffix)

morphemeAnalysis.issue: M-W shows capax (adjective form) not cap (verb stem)
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: Latin capacitas derives from capax (able to hold), which nominalizes as capacitas (quality of being capable). The 'ac' in 'acity' is part of the root form 'capac-' (from capax), not a suffix component. English 'capacity' shows this as cap-acity, visually grouping it as cap + acity, but etymologically it should be capac- (from capax) + -ity
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should be 'capac + ity' (with capac- as nominalization stem from adjective capax)
morphemeAnalysis.detailed_breakdown: capax → capac- (adjective stem) + -itas (quality suffix) → capacitas → English capacity

capacity.notes: This is a KEY FINDING: -ity suffix words derive from adjectives, requiring the adjective stem (capax → capac-), not the verb stem (cap-). Family currently shows verb stem + acity, which is structurally wrong.

captivity.mwEtymology: Late Latin captivitas (from captivus 'taken captive' + -itas suffix)

morphemeAnalysis.issue: Etymology goes through adjective captivus (captive), not directly from cap
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: capere (to take) → captivus (adjective: captive/taken) → captivitas (quality of being captive) → English captivity. The 'tiv' part represents the participial suffix that creates the adjective, then -itas creates the quality nominal. Family shows 'cap + tivity' which misses the intermediate adjective stage.
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should properly show: cap + -tivus → captiv- (adjective stem) + -ity, or at minimum recognize that 'tiv' is not simply a suffix but part of derived adjective form

captivity.notes: Another cap-family word showing same pattern: -ity words derive from adjectives, not directly from verb stems.

morphemeAnalysis.issue: Family shows 'fer + tility' but should show adjective form 'fertil-'
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: ferre (to bear/carry) → fertilis (adjective: fruitful) → fertilitas (quality of being fertile) → English fertility. The breakdown should reflect 'fertil-' (adjective stem) + '-ity', not 'fer + tility'
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should show: fertil + -ity (where fertil- is adjective stem from ferre)

fertility.notes: Pattern continues: -ity words require adjective stems, not verb stems.

morphemeAnalysis.status: ✗ INCORRECT - Missing adjective stem and likely incorrect prefix handling
morphemeAnalysis.issue: Should show in- + fertil + -ity, not in- + fer + tility
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: in- (prefix: not) + fertilis (adjective: fruitful) → infertilis (adjective: not fruitful) → infertilitas → English infertility. Morpheme breakdown should be: in + fertil + ity
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should be 'in + fertil + ity' with 'fertil-' as adjective stem

infertility.notes: Prefix correctly identified (in-) but root still shows verb stem (fer) instead of adjective stem (fertil)

tenacity.mwEtymology: Latin tenacitas (from tenax 'holding fast, persistent' + -itas suffix)

morphemeAnalysis.status: ✗ INCORRECT - Should use adjective stem tenac-
morphemeAnalysis.issue: Family shows 'ten + acity' but should show 'tenac + ity'
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: tenere (to hold) → tenax (adjective: holding fast/persistent) → tenacitas (quality of holding fast) → English tenacity. Root form should be 'tenac-' (from adjective tenax), not 'ten-' (from verb tenere)
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should be 'tenac + ity' where 'tenac-' is the adjective stem

tenacity.notes: Clear pattern: adjective stem (tenax → tenac-) + -ity, not verb stem.

morphemeAnalysis.status: ✗ INCORRECT - Should use adjective stem versatul-/versatil-
morphemeAnalysis.issue: Family shows 'vert + ility' but should show 'versatil + ity'
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: vertere (to turn) → versatilis (adjective: turning, changeable) → versatilitas (quality of being changeable) → English versatility. Root should be 'versatil-' (adjective stem), not 'vert-' (verb stem)

versatility.notes: Same pattern across all -ity words: adjective stem + -ity, not verb stem + -ity

diversity.mwEtymology: Latin diversitas (from diversus 'turned different ways, various' + -itas suffix)

morphemeAnalysis.status: ✗ INCORRECT - Should use diversus stem or show di + vers + ity
morphemeAnalysis.issue: Family shows 'di + vert + ity' but diversus is adjective form, should be 'di + vers + ity' or 'divers + ity'
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: di- + vertere (to turn) → diversus (adjective: turned aside, different) → diversitas (quality of being different) → English diversity. The root in the -ity form should be 'divers-' (adjective stem), and breakdown should reflect 'di + vers + ity' not 'di + vert + ity'
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should be 'di + vers + ity' (with 'vers-' being the participial/adjective stem, different from infinitive 'vert-')

diversity.notes: Complex case: di- prefix + vers- (adjective/participial stem) + -ity. Shows need to distinguish vert- (infinitive) vs vers- (participial/adjective stem)

superficiality.mwEtymology: Latin superficialitas (from superficialis 'on the surface' + -itas suffix)

morphemeAnalysis.issue: Family shows 'facere' as root, but superficiality comes through superficies (surface) → superficialis (adjective) → superficialitas
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: facere (to make) → facies (face/surface, noun) → superficies (on the surface, noun) → superficialis (adjective: on the surface) → superficialitas → English superficiality. The breakdown super + fic + ality misses the noun intermediate stage (facies) and noun → adjective conversion (superficialis)
morphemeAnalysis.correction: More accurate: super + fici + ality or super + ficial + ity (recognizing superficial as adjective form)

superficiality.notes: Complex derivation: shows limitation of simple root-based analysis. Need to track noun and adjective derivations.

specificity.mwEtymology: Latin specificitas (from specificus 'making a kind' + -itas suffix)

morphemeAnalysis.issue: Family shows 'specere' but specificity comes from species (kind) + -ficus (making)
morphemeAnalysis.explanation: This is a compound: species (kind) + -ficus (making) → specificus (making kinds) → specificitas (quality of specificity). The breakdown should reflect this compound nature, not just 'spec + ificity'
morphemeAnalysis.correction: Should be recognized as spec + i + fic + ity or species + -fic + -ity (showing compound origin)

specificity.notes: Edge case: specificity is compound of species + ficus, not straightforward spec derivation.

pattern_1.name: -ity suffix words derive from ADJECTIVES, not verbs
pattern_1.description: Unlike -tion words (verbal action nominals), -ity words are quality nominals that derive from adjective forms
examples: capax (adjective: able to hold) → capac- (adjective stem) + -ity → capacity
tenax (adjective: holding fast) → tenac- (adjective stem) + -ity → tenacity
pattern_1.implication: Current family data uses VERB STEMS for -ity words, which is systematically INCORRECT. Need to map verbs to their adjective forms to get correct morpheme breakdowns.

pattern_2.name: Adjective stem ≠ verb stem
pattern_2.description: Root adjectives often have different forms than the corresponding verbs
pattern_2.implication: Cannot map -ity words directly to root families. Must understand which adjective form is used in the -itas nominalization.

pattern_3.name: Latin nominalization suffix: -itas (becomes -ity)
pattern_3.description: Quality nominals use -itas suffix in Latin, not -tion
pattern_3.implication: Consistent pattern across all 23 words, but requires adjective forms

pattern_4.name: Complex derivations need intermediate stages
pattern_4.description: Some -ity words go through multiple derivation stages
pattern_4.implication: Single root family may not capture full etymological path. Need noun and adjective intermediate forms.

batch2_structure_assessment.issue_summary: Family structure uses verb stems for -ity words, but -ity words derive from adjective forms. This is a fundamental structural mismatch, not a variation in representation.
example_corrections_needed: captivity: cap + tivity → captiv + ity (recognizing captivus as adjective form)
infertility: in + fer + tility → in + fertil + ity
diversity: di + vert + ity → di + vers + ity
